## Introduction

For Lab9 the New York Times API endpoint that I plan to use to complete this assignment is the Top Stories endpoint. The question that I would like to answer is what are the Top 5 most recent Top Stories. The way I plan on accomplishing this is by the HTTR2 data set which is recommended for working with modern API's. While not with R specifically, I do have some experience using API's so I do not anticipate having much trouble with this project. I will update my conclusion if there are anything changes.

```{r }
install.packages("usethis")
```

```{r load-packages}
library(usethis)
library(httr2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
```

```{r create-env-file}
usethis::edit_r_environ()

```

```{r get-api-key}
api_key <- Sys.getenv("MY_API_KEY")
api_secret <- Sys.getenv("MY_API_SECRET")
```

```{r web-scrap}
req <- request("https://api.nytimes.com/svc/topstories/v2/science.json") |> req_url_query('api-key' = api_key)


req <-  req_perform(req)

data <- resp_body_json(req)
data <- data$results
data[1] <- NULL
data[2]<- NULL
data[3] <- NULL

articles <- data$results

articles_clean <- map_dfr(data, function(article) {
  tibble(
    section = article$section,
    subsection = article$subsection,
    title = article$title,
    abstract = article$abstract,
    url = article$url,
    byline = article$byline,
    published_date = article$published_date,
    updated_date = article$updated_date,
    item_type = article$item_type,
    keywords = paste(unlist(article$des_facet), collapse = ", "),
    organizations = paste(unlist(article$org_facet), collapse = ", "),
    people = paste(unlist(article$per_facet), collapse = ", "),
    locations = paste(unlist(article$geo_facet), collapse = ", ")
  )
})

articles_clean <- articles_clean %>% mutate(
  published_date = as.Date(published_date)
)
articles_clean <- articles_clean %>% mutate(
  updated_date = as.Date(updated_date)
)

articles_clean <- articles_clean %>% select(section, title, abstract, byline, published_date)

head(articles_clean, n=10)
```

```{r most-recent}

articles_clean %>%
  arrange(desc(published_date)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  select(title, byline, published_date)
```

# Conclusion 

In conclusion, the endpoint that I chose to use was the Top Stories, specifically the Science endpoint. I stored my api key in a in an renviron file, but committed an example renviron file because that would be used if someone wanted to copy my code. The GET API call was not that difficult to work with, however cleaning the tibble presented a bit of challenge in understanding the format. Since it was a nested JSON object, cleaning was not as straight forward as I was used to. For cleaning, I converted the published date and updated_date into Date variables and provided names for every columns, and lastly I only selected the variables that were necessary, to keep the tibble clean. Ultimately I was able to show the 5 most recently published Science Top Stories.
